newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BRONDBY SCORE STUNNING UPSET WIN OVER KARLSRUHE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRONDBY SCORE STUNNING UPSET WIN OVER KARLSRUHE.

text.p: Brondby of Denmark spectacularly knocked Karlsruhe out of the UEFA Cup on Tuesday after overturning a first leg defeat to win the away leg 5-0 and qualify for the last eight 6-3 on aggregate.

The result was one of the most astonishing of the entire season as Karlsruhe seemed to have the tie won after 77 minutes of the first leg when they led Brondy 3-0. But Ruben Bagger's last minute goal for Brondby in that match, gave the Danes a slight chance -- which they fully exploited in front of 21,000 stunned Germans.

Bagger put his side right back in the tie when he scored the opening goal of the second leg after 41 minutes, suddenly finding space on the edge of the penalty area and driving the ball low and hard past goalkeeper Claus Reitmaier's right hand. That made it Karlsuhe 3, Brondby 2 on aggregate, but the Germans superiority did not last for much longer.
Karlsruhe appeared still to be in shock two minutes later when Dan Egger was left completely unmarked on the six-yard line at a corner and slotted home easily to make it 3-3 on aggregate.
In the second half Brondby maintained their dominance against Karlsruhe who clearly lacked the creative inspiration of Thomas Haessler, out with a broken ankle.

The tie finally turned Brondby's way when Kim Vilfort scored to put the Danes 4-3 ahead on aggregate after 59 minutes. After some sustained German pressure, Peter Moeller put the tie out of therir reach scoring twice in seven minutes, the last goal an impressive long shot from close to the half-way line.

Brondby ended the first half of the Danish season, which has just closed down for the winter, as leaders in the title race, and will hardly fear any of their potential opponents in the quarter-finals next March.
